newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London steady, await jobs figures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London steady, await jobs figures.

text.p: U.S. shares were steady on Thursday as many European investors stayed on the sidelines ahead of Friday's U.S. unemployment data, dealers said.
"There hasn't been a lot of business this morning. The market is just ticking over," one market maker said. "We probably won't see much activity until the jobs numbers are out of the way."

The U.S. non-farm payroll total is expected to rise by 221,000 in May while average hourly earnings are forecast to increase by 0.4 percent during the month, according to a Reuters poll of economists.
A spike in the average wage component could prompt the U.S. Federal Reserve to push up its short-term funds rate following its regular monetary meeting next month, dealers said.
U.S. treasuries were slightly easier with the June T-bond down 4/32 to 110-10/32. The yield on the benchmark 30-year long bond stood at 6.90 percent by 1035 GMT.
Eli Lilly & Co slipped $1/2 to $92-5/8 after press reports said the company may have to write off a large portion of its $4.1 billion acquisition of PCS Health Systems Inc.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that in a recent government filing, Lilly said it was evaluating whether PCS, which it acquired in 1994, was worth "significantly less" than originally believed.
Intel Corp led a generally firmer high-tech sector, gaining $1 to $142-1/2 after dropping $2-1/2 in New York on Wednesday.
Computer makers and related companies saw their share prices fall in New York overnight on rumours that PC manufacturer Gateway 2000 Inc would warn of an earnings shortfall on Thursday.
Gateway said on Wednesday it had no plans to preview its second quarter earnings on Thursday. Gateway traded after hours in New York at $61-3/4, up from $60-3/4 at the close.
IBM was up $1/2 to $82-3/8 while Compaq added $1/4 to $97-7/8.
The June S&P 500 futures contract was up 0.65 to 842.75.
